name: Bright apartment in Ixelles/Louise
description:
You will love this bright apartment in Ixelles. Your own apartment in a traditional house. In a very cool and calm street. Very close to everything to visit Brussels (by foot, by subway, by tramway).

You will be very next to restaurants, cinema, park your car or bike, shopping, etc.
The historic part of Brussel (Grand Place, etc.) is less than 25 mins by foot and all the public transports (trams, bus..) are 5 mins by foot from our house ..

The best way to know more ? Check our reviews !
neighborhood_overview:
You will be in a very silent and little street but, Avenue Louise is just on the corner !

Avenue Louise was recently nominated, in january 2012, the 8th Avenue the more friendly in the world ! Before Avenue des Champs Elysées (Paris) and 5th Avenue (New York) !

But you are also very close to typical areas in Brussels (Grand Place, Sablon, Place Saint Boniface, Matonge, Flagey) where you can relax and enjoy your stay.
host_about:
I'm actor mostly for theater but also movies and television. I'm often outside on evening time and I rent the second floor of my house recently renovated (outside & inside).

I try to care my guests on the best way, giving informations and good links on Brussel. 

If you send your request with picture of you, information of the purpose of your trip : it is a must !

You're welcome,

Pierre

name: Charming & cosy B&B in Uccle.
description: Located in a warmly house, very quite and nicely decoreted with south of France colored accents. A lovely garden where you can have a rest at sun on a deck chair or having your breakfast. One of the most well known district of Brussels for shopping, situated very near beautiful parks for walks and some nice restaurants. It takes 5mn by tram to get to the Commune of Saint Gilles for more restaurants, bars and cafes.
neighborhood_overview:
Located very near from the Commune of Saint Gilles, by tram 51 takes 5mn, where you find many nice restaurants, wine-beer bars and cafes.
I recommande you Le BAR du MATIN (http://bardumatin.blogspot.be)
Chaussé d'Alsemberg, 172. Tram exit: Albert.
With a big terrace outside at sun, nice inside, delicious fruit juices, breakfast and snack food, concerts music organized.
There's always a good reason to share a good moment at Bar du matin !

Also, beautiful nice parks around for walks and shops.
host_about:
De nature très sociable et spontanée, j'aime rencontrer de nouvelles personnes et à cette occasion, de nouveaux liens d'amitiés peuvent se créer. 
Comme je suis passionnée de voyages, j'ai toujours un grand plaisir à recevoir à la maison des hôtes étrangers à qui je réserve un accueil bien chaleureux dans ma jolie demeure bruxelloise.
La cuisine, le jardinage, les activités culturelles qui ne manquent pas à Bruxelles font partie de mes hobbies préférés.

Self-contained studio on the 2nd floor. Ideal for recharging your batteries! High ceilings, 1 small kitchen area, 1 shower room with private WC. 140x200 bed on mezzanine. Central heating. Velux view of nature.

name: Charming townhouse with workspaces & garden
description:
Welcome to our charming 1904 Belgian townhouse, nestled in the picturesque Village du 'Chien Vert' (Green Dog), one of Brussels' greenest and most enchanting areas. This semi-pedestrian haven offers the perfect blend of tranquility and convenience, ideal for both leisure and work visits. Just moments away from the vibrant city center, the EU district, and the majestic Forêt de Soignes, you can experience the best of Brussels right from your doorstep!

neighborhood_overview:
Village-like neighbourhood, restaurants, including two Michelin-star restaurants, bars at about 15 minutes from the European district.

Gorgeous parc on the other side of the boulevard – one of the largest in Brussels –, hosting a little wilde-life of its own, with a beautiful running/bike path connecting the South area of Brussels.

A 5-minute walk takes you to the famous Tram museum where you can hop on a 1935 tram for a beautiful little ride around Brussels.

A 5-minute car ride takes you to Sonian Wood, for beautiful and quiet stolls in one of the most beautiful forests in Belgium.

A 10-minute car ride takes you to Tervuren and its Africa Museum

Museum lovers will also have an easy access to the Royal Museums of Art and History (10-minute tram ride), or to the automobile and army museum by the well-known Cinquantenaire.

neighborhood_overview:
Rue des Minimes (Miniemenstraat in Dutch) is a street in Brussels that goes from the rue du Faucon to the Place du Grand Sablon. Until 1895 it gave in the picturesque rue du Coq-d'Inde which debouched on the place of Sablon but which was razed to allow the street of Minimes to reach there directly.

It owes its current name to the Minimes, who built their convent there in 1621. Both its name and its length have varied over the centuries. In the fourteenth century, it was called Blaerstrate, it should have been a Jean Blaes who lived there around 1300. In a document of 1374, it is also called Super Zabulum against Obbruxellam versus (Where we go from Sablon to Saint-Gilles). This long artery joined the southern end of Laines Street. In the 17th century, the northern part took the name of rue des Minimes, while its southern section took the name of rue des Marolles, a corrupt form of the name of a religious order that was established there, the Sisters of Mary or Mariam Colente

Why Anderlecht ?
Anderlecht, home of Belgium’s most famous soccer team is the best kept secret of Brussels. Only 15 minutes by metro from Brussels bustling heart and yet a stone throw away from the “Pajottenland”, the beautifull countryside immortalized in Breughel’s famous paintings. Discover the Erasmus house, a 16th century mansion dedicated to one of Europe’s finest philosophers. Or pay a visit to the miller of the” Luizenmolen”, an authentic wooden windmill still in function. Take a bike ride to the castle of Gaasbeek, the Versailles of Brussels, and enjoy a Geuze beer in the tavern “Graaf Egmond”, a popular outing on a sunny day. And if you prefer an easy ride close to the waterside, you can cycle to the picturesque town of Halle, alongside the canal.

description:
Not your ordinary hotel in Brussels; the only hotel in Brussels for the UNORDINARY

Located a few minutes from the famous Grand Place in Brussels, Hotel La Grande Cloche is a trendy and offbeat boutique hotel.

Completely renovated in 2019, the hotel is still the oldest operating hotel in Brussels.

La Grande Cloche is also a restaurant, Klok, where hotel guests meet the people of Brussels around a homeade & local food.
neighborhood_overview:
The first station on the Brussels-Mons line, the Bogards station was built in 1840 in the city centre, 400 metres from the Grand-Place. Located on the site of the former Bogards convent, on the site of the current Place Rouppe.

As you have understood, “La Grande Cloche” refers to the bell used for the departure of trains, which rang from what is now the hotel reception!

The industrial development of the 19th century led to the decision to move the station out of downtown Brussels. Its demolition in 1864 offered the opportunity to clean up the district, and to build a majestic avenue on the site of the abandoned roads: the Drève du Midi, the current Avenue de Stalingrad.

In the mid-1990s, the Gare du Midi hosted the TGV (Paris-Bruxelles/Brussel-Köln – Amsterdam) and the Eurostar terminal. On this occasion, an urban development operation was launched to take advantage of the “TGV effect” and allow the neighbourhood to be renovated.

description: The adventure of this apartment was born from the desire to travel differently: far from fixed stays, standardized establishments and marked routes. neighborhood_overview:
If Paris has its Saint-Germain-des-Prés, Brussels has the Brugmann, Vert Chasseur and Fort-Jaco districts, which designate a city within the city, a few hundred meters from Avenue Louise and the Bois de la Camber. A district that shines with its dynamism thanks to its art galleries, new shops, wine bars and restaurants.
What is striking when strolling through these quiet streets, lined with beautiful Brussels houses that are often centuries old, is this village atmosphere in the city. This neighborhood on a human scale, although very inhabited, offers the advantage of not being invaded by offices.

neighborhood_overview:
If Paris has its Saint-Germain-des-Prés, Brussels has the Brugmann district, which designates the few streets around the eponymous square, a few hundred meters from Avenue Louise. A village in the city that shines with dynamism thanks to its art galleries, new shops, wine bars and restaurants.
What strikes you when you stroll through these quiet streets, lined with beautiful Brussels houses, often centuries-old, is this village atmosphere in the city. This human-sized neighborhood, although very crowded, offers the advantage of not being crowded with offices.
There are indeed small shops in boho mode, a park, a square and a slightly Parisian and relaxed atmosphere. Here, everything invites you to feel out of the city: shops, restaurants are welcoming and no big chain has come to spoil the landscape. name: Lovely room in a spacious apartment with bathtub.
description:
In the trendy Saint-Gilles neighborood, at the second floor of a three apartments building with elevator.

The place is big and has wooden floor, a fully equipped kitchen, a big bathroom with bathtub and a separate shower, two toilets & a laundry.

Fast wifi, bluetooth hifi speakers & Italian coffee machine.

The guests room is quiet and luminous.

Saint-Gilles is IMHO the best location to visit Brussels. The Midi Train Station is very near (5min by metro).

I also have a very gentle cat.
neighborhood_overview:
Saint-Gilles is a hip arty yet quiet neighborood in Brussels.

The Parvis de Saint-Gilles with its bars and restaurants is at 5min walk.

The chic area for shopping, Avenue Louise/Avenue de la Toison d'Or, is at 3min. walk.

The hip second-hand shops and the daily flea market (Place du Jeu de Balle) are at 15min. walk.

The Sablon area with its wonderful ´Petit Sablon', its antique dealers and high end chocolate/pastry shops is also at 15 min. walk.

You are at 25 min. by foot from the Grand Place and the Art Nouveau - Musée Horta.

There is a good pastry shop, a good bakery and a supermarket very close to my place.

The metro stations, the tram and bus stops are at 3min walk.

For the European institution folks: by public transport, the Schuman area is at 20min and the Madou area is at 10min.

If all the stars are aligned, you can get to Zaventem airport by public transports in approx. 40min

The European District of Brussels (Quartier Européen in French) comprises the headquarters of the European Parliament, the Council of Ministers and the European Commission.
Before becoming the European District, the neighborhood was a tranquil residential area. The immense buildings are bounded by three larges green spaces to the east of the city: Parc de Bruxelles (Brussels Park), the Cinquantenaire (park and palace) and Leopold Park.
One of the most famous landmarks of the European Union is the Berlaymont building that houses the headquarters of the European Commission. The fourteen-story building was founded in 1967 and is in the shape of an X.
The Place du Luxembourg is also the place to be on Thursday night to hangout in a cosmopolitan atmosphere.

Just steps away from the iconic statue of the little boy, a symbol of Brussels' spirit, you will find a maze of cobbled streets lined with shops, artisanal chocolate makers, and cozy cafes.

This neighborhood is also renowned for its proximity to the Grand Place, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, where stunning Gothic and Baroque architecture will leave you in awe. Stroll through historic galleries, savor local specialties like Belgian waffles or fries, and enjoy the welcoming terraces that bring the streets to life.

In the evening, the area comes alive with restaurants serving traditional dishes and inviting bars where you can sample Belgium's famous beers. Whether you're a fan of culture, gastronomy, or simply seeking an authentic Brussels experience, the Manneken Pis district is sure to charm you.

You’ll find plenty of unique shops, from antique dealers to vintage clothing stores. For food lovers, there’s also a great selection of restaurants and brasseries offering both traditional dishes and modern cuisine. A stroll through the neighborhood always holds pleasant surprises! Plus, the Sablon, famous for its high-end antique shops and chocolatiers, and the Grand Place are just a short walk away, making it easy to explore more of Brussels' historic charm. Not far from there, you’ll also find the Mont des Arts area, home to several renowned museums. A perfect route for discovering the city's artistic and culinary delights!
